packageRules.description: The oldest Paper the plugins support. Raising it drops every server still on it, so it's changed by hand. The newest Paper is tracked by .github/workflows/minecraft.yml.
The test-only database drivers stay at the versions Paper ships, so tests run the drivers servers have. Bumped by hand with Paper's.

xPlots compiles against the newest WorldGuard and WorldEdit built for Java 21 (xplots/build.gradle.kts). Later ones are Java 25 class files, which JDK 21 can't read, so they're bumped by hand when the build moves to Java 25.
The oldest Bukkit API the rewrite runs on (spigot-floor in gradle/libs.versions.toml), which the core's Java shim compiles against so it uses nothing newer. It's the floor, never bumped.
Third-party actions run with the repo's secrets, so they're pinned to a commit (CodeQL flags tags, which can be moved); Renovate keeps the pins current. GitHub's own actions stay on tags.
CI builds, tests and boots every plugin, and merging releases nothing, so small updates merge themselves once it passes. Majors wait for a review.

The rewrite's Kotlin (gradle/libs.versions.toml). Servers before 1.15 share the first Xena plugin's stdlib, so every plugin moves to a new Kotlin together, by hand (DECISIONS.md). The stdlib is downloaded at runtime and checked against its SHA-256 in gradle/library-pins.txt, so the build fails until the bump also updates that (-PupdatePins).

xBackup downloads these when an SFTP or FTP remote is used, and checks each jar against the SHA-256 in xbackup/src/main/java/co/xenastudios/xbackup/remote/Libraries.java, which LibrariesTest compares with this version. A bump needs the new hash too, so it gets its own pull request, merged by hand. Last, so it wins over the automerge rule above.
